title: Technology Sector Update for 10/12/2018: FB,BILI,IMOS,LDOS,LLL,AIR - Nasdaq.com
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT +3.61%
AAPL +3.50%
IBM +1.31%
CSCO +3.77%
GOOG +2.77%
Technology stocks easily outpaced other sectors on Friday, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were adding over 3.2% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising more than 1.9%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Facebook ( FB ) dropped over 1% at one point on Friday after the social network company lowered the number of users it believes were affected by a security breach first reported last month. The company Friday said around 30 million users had their access tokens stolen in the cyber-hacking incident, down from the 50 million Facebook user initially thought to have been affected in the automated process that grew from a relatively small set of accounts already controlled by the hackers and eventually spreading to around 30 million friends and family members of about 400,000 users.
In other sector news:
(+) Bilibili ( BILI ) jumped out to a more than 9% advance at one point on Friday after the Chinese online entertainment platform signed a a strategic partnership with the Houston Rockets of the NBA to expand the basketball team's eSports presence. Under the new tie-up, Bilibili becomes the official partner of Clutch Gaming, the Rockets' eSports team, and the Clutch Gaming team will broadcast their games in real time on the Bilibili platform.
(+) ChipMOS Technologies ( IMOS ) was maintaining most its nearly 4% gain on Friday after the specialty chipmaker said it has filed a capital reduction request with the Nasdaq Stock Market, seeking approval of ITS plan to return about TWD1.5, or about $0.05, to investors for each of their American depositary shares.
(-) Leidos Innovations ( LDOS ) was nearly 1% lower in afternoon trading, giving back a 2% gain earlier Friday that followed the cybersecurity and data management company being selected to share in a $25.5 billion, 10-year contract to supply global logistics and related support services for the U.S. Department of Defense, the Pentagon said late Thursday. Several other companies are participating in the project, including L-3 Technologies ( LLL ) and AAR Corp (AIR), the Defense Department said, adding work locations and funding will be determined with each order.
